ask: Why is it on the path?
cards: From the capture of Ceuta in 1415 to Goa, Malacca and Hormuz, Portugal built an empire of fortified trading posts rather than territory.
Henry's sponsorship of voyages down the West African coast turned exploration from episodic raiding into an institutionalised commercial enterprise.
Da Gama's arrival at Calicut in 1498 completed the sea route to Asia that Bartolomeu Dias had opened by rounding the Cape.
The treaty of 1494 fixed a meridian dividing newly discovered lands between the Spanish and Portuguese spheres.
Columbus, Cortés and Pizarro made Spain master of the Americas, and under Philip II the first empire on which the sun never set.
Plantation economies such as Brazil's sugar estates rested on the forced transport of enslaved Africans across the Atlantic.
A small republic projected power across four continents by seizing maritime chokepoints such as Malacca, taken from Portugal in 1641.
Founded in 1602 with permanent capital, tradable shares and powers to wage war and make treaties, the VOC was something new.
Built on a fiscal-military state and a professional Royal Navy, it became the largest empire in history, ruling roughly a quarter of the world's population.
